column5: Comment Text
Honest question — how do we know the money actually goes to treatment? I want to help but there are so many scam campaigns on Facebook right now

I had the same concern so I actually went through the whole page before donating. They list the specific hospital (Mass General), specific diagnosis (IDH-wildtype GBM grade IV), and the cost breakdown is itemized per treatment. It's not a generic 'help me' page. I donated $25

my sister is a nurse at Dana-Farber and confirmed that dendritic cell therapy in Germany is a real protocol that US insurance won't cover. the costs listed on the page are consistent with what families actually pay. I donated
I was skeptical too but the medical updates with actual MRI results and dates convinced me. scam pages never have that level of detail. donated $20

My husband died of glioblastoma at 47. We tried everything the US healthcare system offered — surgery, radiation, temodar. Median survival is 14 months and he made it 16. If this treatment had existed and been accessible he might still be here. Donated $50. Please share this

so sorry for your loss. my best friend had the same diagnosis two years ago. made it 13 months. the US healthcare system essentially tells you to go home and get your affairs in order. if there's a treatment out there that could change that, we should all chip in
lost my mom the same way. the helplessness of knowing the standard treatment isn't enough is the worst feeling in the world. at least now there's something beyond chemo. donated

I'm a neurology resident. The study they cite (Human Vaccines & Immunotherapeutics 2025) is legitimate — 68% increase in median overall survival for GBM patients who received dendritic cell vaccines. Particularly relevant for IDH-wildtype with unmethylated MGMT which is what Emily has. The problem is the FDA classifies it as experimental which means no insurance covers it. It's available in Germany on a private-pay basis. The science is real
thank you for explaining this. I wasn't sure if the 68% number was real or exaggerated. donated now
the fact that the FDA can take 5-10 years to approve treatments that are already saving lives in Europe is everything wrong with American healthcare in one sentence

She's 21. She wanted to become a doctor to help people. Now she's learning what it means to be a patient. That quote broke me. I can't imagine being her age and hearing you have 14 months to live unless you can raise $150,000 for treatment your insurance refuses to cover. Donated
that line about 'every donation isn't just money, it's time' made me cry. donated immediately
done ✅ and shared. if everyone scrolling past this donated even $5 she'd be in Germany within the month
As a mom of a 20 year old daughter in pre-med this hit me so hard I couldn't scroll past it. She could be my daughter. Donated $30 and shared with everyone I know
shared with my whole family group chat. my daughter is 22 and in nursing school. these things make you hold your kids a little tighter
the American healthcare system in one story: the treatment exists, the science proves it works, but if you can't pay $150,000 out of pocket you just die. donated and absolutely disgusted
and then people wonder why Americans are crowdfunding their healthcare. this shouldn't be a GoFundMe situation. but until the system changes, it is. donated $15
we spend more per capita on healthcare than any country in the world and a 21 year old has to beg strangers online to afford treatment that could save her life. unbelievable
small donation but every bit counts. praying for you Emily. you're going to be an incredible doctor someday ❤️
done. my college roommate was diagnosed with a brain tumor at 23. he's in remission now thanks to experimental treatment that insurance initially denied. never give up Emily

I went to the page and what convinced me was how transparent the cost breakdown is. Dendritic cell therapy $55k, proton beam $40k, profiling $12k, travel $30k — every dollar accounted for. that's not how scams work
exactly. the updates showing actual MRI results with dates sealed it for me. this is real. donated
donated $20. not much but if 7,500 people give $20 she's there. share this and make it happen
donated in memory of my sister who we lost to brain cancer in 2022. she was a teacher. 36 years old. if a treatment exists that gives even a few more years of life it's worth fighting for

I'm a BU student and hearing about Emily's diagnosis sent shockwaves through our whole program. The pre-med association organized a fundraiser. If you're reading this and you can spare even $5, please donate. She's one of us
